item.text:
{"record":{"id":"REQ-RUN-0001","title":"Repository layout: one workspace and its library crates","status":"Active","version":"1.0.0","created":"2026-09-19","last_updated":"2026-09-20","owner":"randlee","supersedes":null,"superseded_by":null,"requirement_statement":{"text":"The GitHub repository `randlee/sc-runtime` MUST contain one Cargo workspace,
declared in the root `Cargo.toml`.

The workspace members MUST be exactly these library crates. Amended 2026-10-25 ([ADR-RUN-0012](architecture.md), [ADR-RUN-0013](architecture.md)): `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` and `sc-cron` are members. Amended 2026-11-11 (PRD-STO-3): `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` holds the atm-core SQLite writer that sits behind `Storage<T>`; the earlier rule that it is not a store the daemon opens and not a template dependency is withdrawn. The generated daemon may depend on `sc-cron` only through the optional `cron` feature fixed by [REQ-RUN-0301](requirements.md); feature-off generated builds do not link it.

| Member path | Crate name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/sc-config` | `sc-config` | JSON config files with environment overrides |
| `crates/sc-transport` | `sc-transport` | UDS/TCP listener and client connector |
| `crates/sc-command` | `sc-command` | response envelope, `OpError`, REST and MCP conversions |
| `crates/sc-runtime` | `sc-runtime` | daemon assembly: `Daemon::builder()`, `daemon.lock`, `DaemonFixture` |
| `crates/sc-runtime-db-sqlite` | `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` | rusqlite write actor; one connection, one thread |
| `crates/sc-cron` | `sc-cron` | SQLite-backed cron; the app registers the job |
| `crates/sc-cron-commands` (Phase C target) | `sc-cron-commands` | optional standard cron DTOs and scheduler adapter; ADR-RUN-0019 |

Phase C amendment: the new adapter member is planned, not yet implemented.
Its default DTO graph and optional scheduler edge are defined by
REQ-RUN-0332 and NFR-CRNC-0001; no reverse core command/runtime edge is allowed.

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `template/` | the `cargo-generate` template root, including `template/cargo-generate.toml`, `template/AGENTS.md.j2` and `template/CLAUDE.md.j2` |
| `wizard/` | `wizard.json`, `answers.schema.json` (the options contract), `pages/` (wizard HTML pages), `fixtures/` (one answers JSON file per tested variant) |
| `scripts/` | `new_project.py` (the generation driver) and `run_wizard.py` |
| `tests/unit/` | contract tests for the generator: schema validity, key-set match, invalid fixtures failing closed |
| `examples/spike/` | the throwaway spike; present only until the `v0.1.0` tag ([REQ-RUN-0103](requirements.md)) |
| `docs/` | requirements and architecture files; the ADRs are sections of the architecture files (see below) |
| `boundaries/` | one directory per library crate holding its `sc-lint-boundary` manifest ([REQ-RUN-0005](requirements.md)) |
| `Justfile` | the `just` recipes, including `just new <dest>` |
| `.github/workflows/` | crate CI and the template fixture-matrix CI |

Nothing under `wizard/` or `scripts/` may be placed inside `template/`, so
that no generated project ever contains a wizard or driver file. This item
owns that rule; items about the wizard or the driver refer to it.

Decided in this document: ADRs live in the architecture files (`docs/architecture.md` and `docs/<crate>/architecture.md`).

`examples/spike` is an excluded standalone package while it exists. It is not
a fifth workspace member and it is not a Cargo example. Root `Cargo.toml`
`exclude` names `examples/spike`. The workspace member list is exactly the
library crates in the table above. Sprint a-5 deleted `crates/sc-command/lint-edge/`
when `crates/sc-runtime` landed. `sc-observability` and `sc-observability-otlp`
are not workspace members. `cargo tree` enforces those edges, because sc-lint
0.8.0 rejects a forbidden edge whose target is absent.

The files in `template/` contain `cargo-generate` placeholders and do not compile until rendered.","statements":[{"modal":"Must","text":"The GitHub repository `randlee/sc-runtime` MUST contain one Cargo workspace, declared in the root `Cargo.toml`."},{"modal":"Must","text":"The workspace members MUST be exactly these library crates. (see table above)"},{"modal":"Must","text":"The repository root MUST contain each directory and file listed in the second table in the Requirement Statement (the table headed `Path | Contents`), except that `examples/spike/` is exempt at and after the `v0.1.0` tag."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"Each directory and file in the path table MUST NOT be a workspace member."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"`template/` MUST NOT be a workspace member."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"`template/` MUST NOT be matched by a workspace `members` glob."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"The repository MUST NOT contain the sc-runtime design's unused `docs/adr/` directory."}]},"rationale":"Keeping the crates and the template in one repository means a crate API
change and the template change that follows it land in one pull request, and
template CI can test the template against the crates at the same commit. How
a generated project is pointed at the checked-out crates is not decided here:
it is the `[patch.crates-io]` question recorded as OPEN in
[REQ-RUN-0003](requirements.md). Keeping `template/` out of the workspace
keeps `cargo build --workspace` working, because the template's Rust files
are not valid Rust until rendered.","success_criteria":{"text":"1. Inspect the root `Cargo.toml`: `[workspace] members` is the glob `crates/*`.
   A missing directory is not a member. At the close of sprint `b-1` the glob
   resolves to `crates/sc-config`, `crates/sc-transport`, `crates/sc-command`,
   `crates/sc-runtime`, and `crates/sc-runtime-db-sqlite`. Sprint `b-3` adds
   `crates/sc-cron` and does not edit `Cargo.toml`. The member set is then
   the six crates in the table above.
   `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` lists those packages and
   lists no package whose manifest path is under `template/`. Amended
   2026-10-25.
2. `cargo build --workspace` run at the repository root exits 0 and compiles
   no file under `template/`.
3. Each path in the second table exists at the repository root (with
   `examples/spike/` exempt at and after the `v0.1.0` tag).
4. `find template -path '*wizard*' -o -name 'new_project.py' -o -name
   'run_wizard.py'` prints nothing.
5. `test -d docs/adr` fails (the directory does not exist), and

{"record":{"id":"REQ-RUN-0004","title":"Root `justfile` recipes `lint`, `test` and `new`","status":"Active","version":"1.0.0","created":"2026-09-19","last_updated":"2026-09-20","owner":"randlee","supersedes":null,"superseded_by":null,"requirement_statement":{"text":"Definitions: SC base commands are the standard lint and test recipe names supplied by the sc-lint tooling adopted in this repository. A recipe is a named Justfile command. The three base recipes are the three rows in the recipe table below. The SC base command names are the primary sc-lint-supplied Justfile recipe names lint and test.

The SC base command names `lint` and `test` are the recipe names that `sc-lint init --just` writes. The first line stays the sc-lint initialization header.

| Recipe | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `just lint` | Runs every static check for this repository and exits non-zero if any check fails. It MUST include the `sc-lint-boundary` check ([REQ-RUN-0005](requirements.md)) and the `sc-lint` source file length check, 1000 source lines not counting blank and comment-only lines ([NFR-RUN-0008](requirements.md)). |
| `just test` | Runs every command of the `just test` list below, and exits non-zero if any of them fails. |
| `just new <dest>` | Runs the generation driver `scripts/new_project.py` with `<dest>` as the destination directory of the new project. Any further arguments (for example `--var-file <answers.json>` or `--prefill <json>`) MUST be passed through to the driver unchanged. |

The test command list is specified in this record; the sc-runtime design names only the recipe.

1. `cargo test --workspace --exclude sc-cron` (Monty needs rustc 1.96; see items 2 and 6).
2. `cargo test -p sc-cron` with default features.
3. `cargo test -p sc-config`, `cargo test -p sc-transport`,
   `cargo test -p sc-command` and `cargo test -p sc-runtime`, each with
   default cargo features. These are needed because `cargo test --workspace`
   builds `sc-transport` and `sc-command` once with their `server` feature
   on (`sc-runtime` enables it, and cargo unifies features across the
   packages it builds together), so it never tests their default-feature
   build.
4. `cargo test -p sc-transport --features server` and
   `cargo test -p sc-command --features server`.
5. The generator contract tests under `tests/unit/`.
6. `cargo test -p sc-cron --features monty` on **rustc 1.96** (the `monty`
   1.4 crates require 1.96; workspace MSRV stays 1.94.1 for the other crates).

There is exactly one recorded exception: the job required by [REQ-RUN-0306](requirements.md), which proves that plain `cargo generate` works without the driver, and therefore runs `cargo generate --path template ...` and `cargo build --workspace` directly.

`just lint` with no profile runs the sc-lint 0.8.6 full profile through
`.sc-lint/bootstrap.py` and `sc-lint.toml`: `sc-lint lint sc-boundary` (the
`boundary` lint), line-counts, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --exclude sc-cron --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and
`cargo clippy -p sc-cron --all-targets --features monty -- -D warnings` on
**rustc 1.96**. `just lint gates`
is the early profile of boundary plus line-counts. The line-counts key is
`[line_counts] max_production_lines` and its value is `1000` for non-test
files under `crates/*/src`. `template/**/*.rs` is not configured in this
sprint.","statements":[{"modal":"Must","text":"The file `Justfile` (capital J) at the root of `randlee/sc-runtime` MUST define the `lint` recipe with the behavior specified in the `just lint` table row."},{"modal":"Must","text":"The file `Justfile` (capital J) at the root of `randlee/sc-runtime` MUST define the `test` recipe with the behavior specified in the `just test` table row."},{"modal":"Must","text":"The file `Justfile` (capital J) at the root of `randlee/sc-runtime` MUST define the `new <dest>` recipe with the behavior specified in the `just new <dest>` table row."},{"modal":"Must","text":"`just test` MUST execute all six numbered entries in this record's test command list."},{"modal":"Must","text":"Decided in this document: every job in `.github/workflows/` that lints, tests or generates MUST do so by calling one of the `lint`, `test` or `new` recipes, not by calling `cargo`, `python` or a lint tool directly."},{"modal":"Must","text":"A workflow file under `.github/workflows/` (the crate CI workflow) MUST run `just lint` and `just test` at the repository root on every pull request."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"`lint` is a standard SC base command name; it MUST NOT be renamed or aliased to another primary name."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"`test` is a standard SC base command name; it MUST NOT be renamed or aliased to another primary name."}]},"rationale":"Every SC repository exposes the same base `just` commands so that agents, CI
and people use one vocabulary and need no per-repository knowledge to lint or
test. Routing CI through the same recipes means a green local `just lint` and
`just test` predicts a green CI run.","success_criteria":{"text":"1. `just --list` at the repository root shows `lint`, `test` and `new`.
2. `just lint` and `just test` each exit 0 on a clean checkout of the default
   branch.
3. Introducing a failing unit test in any workspace crate makes `just test`
   exit non-zero; introducing a failing test under `tests/unit/` does the
   same.
4. Introducing, in `crates/sc-command`, a failing test gated with
   `#[cfg(not(feature = "server"))]` makes `just test` exit non-zero, and so
   does a failing test gated with `#[cfg(feature = "server")]`. This shows
   both feature configurations are tested.
5. `just new <dest> --var-file wizard/fixtures/sqlite-mcp.json` invokes
   `scripts/new_project.py` with that destination and that `--var-file`
   argument (check by inspecting the recipe body).
6. Inspect every file in `.github/workflows/`: each lint, test or generate
   step is a `just lint`, `just test` or `just new` invocation, except the
   steps of the one plain-`cargo generate` job of
   [REQ-RUN-0306](requirements.md).
7. One workflow file under `.github/workflows/` has a `pull_request` trigger
   and steps running `just lint` and `just test` at the repository root, and
   a pull request's check list shows a run of that workflow.","acceptance_criteria":[],"test_evidence":[]},"dependencies":{"text":"","requires":[],"related":[]},"product_applicability":{"text":"","applies_to":[],"does_not_apply_to":[]},"implementation_notes":{"text":"","key_considerations":[]},"test_strategy":{"text":"","test_types":[]},"related_documents":{"text":"","requirements":[],"architecture_decisions":[],"design_documents":[],"work_items":[],"external_references":[]}}}

   criterion does not prescribe the deferred helper or test-generation shape

   [NFR-RUN-0010](requirements.md).

   equal to `null`, and `error` containing `kind`, `code` and `message`.
   Once the present-or-omitted question of
   [REQ-CMD-0002](sc-command/requirements.md) is decided: `error` holds
   exactly the keys defined there. It also asserts the MCP result is flagged
   as an error.
3. Each envelope in criteria 1 and 2 has exactly the keys `version`, `ok`,
   `data`, `error`.

{"record":{"id":"REQ-RUN-0301","title":"Layout of the workspace rendered from `template/`","status":"Active","version":"1.0.0","created":"2026-09-19","last_updated":"2026-11-12","owner":"randlee","supersedes":null,"superseded_by":null,"requirement_statement":{"text":"Definitions: CLI means command-line interface. MCP means Model Context Protocol. HTTP means Hypertext Transfer Protocol. TCP means Transmission Control Protocol. SQL means Structured Query Language. ADR means architecture decision record. The template is the cargo-generate source tree under template/. The rendered local.json is the configuration override file listed in the generated .gitignore. sc-cron/monty is the Monty feature of the sc-cron scheduler crate.

Command paths may be written directly in Phase D. Direct Tcli-to-Tsql conversion needs no custom transform. Later consumer-side generation against the delivered framework remains permitted.

This layout is the interim, hand-written form. `store-sqlite` on sqlx, the per-layout service files and the adaptor crates are not the target; see PRD §3 and §4.

Which crates render follows [REQ-RUN-0326](requirements.md). Package names are `<project>-<role>` ([REQ-RUN-0329](requirements.md)). "v0.1" means the first release, in which the only database option was SQLite and the package names were the role names below. 

```text
<project>/
  Cargo.toml                  # workspace
  crates/
    api-types/                # always; rendered package <project>-types
    schema/                   # when the layout has a store; package <project>-schema
    store-sqlite/             # when the layout includes SQLite
    store-postgres/           # when the layout's engine is Postgres
    store-mysql/              # when the layout's engine is MySQL
```

{"record":{"id":"REQ-CMD-0003","title":"`From<Result<T, OpError>>` for `Envelope<T>`","status":"Active","version":"1.0.0","created":"2026-09-19","last_updated":"2026-09-19","owner":"randlee","supersedes":null,"superseded_by":null,"requirement_statement":{"text":"Definitions: The envelope contract version is the single version supplied by sc-command for the response object with version, ok, data and error fields. Its type and value remain the open item recorded in REQ-CMD-0001; the caller does not supply it.

The crate `sc-command` MUST provide, with default features, the
implementation

```rust
impl<T> From<Result<T, OpError>> for Envelope<T>
```

so that a service result converts with `.into()`. `Envelope<T>` is the
response envelope with JSON keys `version`, `ok`, `data`, `error`
([REQ-CMD-0001](requirements.md)); `OpError` is the typed error
([REQ-CMD-0002](requirements.md)).

| Input | Resulting envelope |
|---|---|
| `Ok(value)` | `ok` is `true`, `data` is `value`, `error` is null |
| `Err(op_error)` | `ok` is `false`, `data` is null, `error` is `op_error` |","statements":[{"modal":"Must","text":"The conversion MUST behave as follows: (see table above)"},{"modal":"Must","text":"In both cases `version` MUST be the crate's single envelope contract version (its type and value are an open item recorded in [REQ-CMD-0001](requirements.md))."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"The caller MUST NOT supply `version`."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"The implementation MUST NOT require any trait bound on `T`."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"The conversion MUST NOT alter `value` or `op_error`."}]},"rationale":"Service functions in a generated project return `Result<T, OpError>`. With
this conversion an axum handler whose return type is `Envelope<Widget>` has a
one-line body, `service::create_widget(&s, input).await.into()`, and no
project writes its own success-or-failure wrapping code.","success_criteria":{"text":"1. A unit test converts `Ok::<Sample, OpError>(sample)` with `.into()` into

   serialises it, and asserts `ok` is `false`, `data` is JSON `null`, and
   `error` equals the serialised `op_error`.
3. A unit test asserts the `version` value is the same in the two envelopes
   above.
4. A test compiles `let _: Envelope<NotSerialize> = Ok(NotSerialize).into();`
   where `NotSerialize` implements no serde trait, proving the conversion
   has no bound on `T`.

Server-feature leakage is activation of server implementation features through the common-helper dependency edges.

{"record":{"id":"NFR-RUN-0003","title":"Standard crates, used the documented way","status":"Active","version":"1.0.0","created":"2026-09-19","last_updated":"2026-11-12","owner":"randlee","supersedes":null,"superseded_by":null,"requirement_statement":{"text":"Definitions: CLI means command-line interface. MCP means Model Context Protocol. HTTP means Hypertext Transfer Protocol. SQL means Structured Query Language. API means application programming interface. ADR means architecture decision record. A building block is a crate used to provide one of the jobs listed in the Job/Crate table. A documented API is an API shown in that crate's documentation for the selected job. A governing requirement or explicit amendment takes precedence over the table's crate choice for a job it specifically addresses.

No command path must be hand-written. A later consumer-side generator may produce that path against the delivered sc-runtime. The existing repo-internal macro policy and its success criteria stand; Phase D builds no generator. The historical generator clause below does not forbid consumer-side command generation.

The prohibited list below was a design recommendation, not an owner requirement, and three of its entries no longer bind as written. (1) "A command or operation registry" does not forbid the shared command path of PRD §3. (2) "A portable query layer" forbids passing SQL across backends; it does not forbid `Storage<T>`, which carries no SQL and is required by PRD-STO-2. (3) "A macro system" and "a code generator of its own" are undecided, not prohibited: the owner is considering an sc-compose or syn-based generator (PRD §9). Success criterion 1 stands until that decision. The prohibition on wrapper types around `axum`, `rmcp` and `sqlx` stands.

The chosen crates are:

| Job | Crate |
|---|---|
| HTTP server and router | `axum` 0.8 |
| MCP server | `rmcp` 3.x (`StreamableHttpService`, `#[tool]`, `#[tool_router]`) |
| OpenAPI | `utoipa` and `utoipa-axum` (`OpenApiRouter`, `routes!`) |
| SQL | `sqlx` 0.9 |
| CLI parsing | `clap` derive |
| HTTP client | `reqwest` 0.13 |
| template rendering | `cargo-generate` |

- a command or operation registry;
- a macro system of its own: no crate with `proc-macro = true`, and no
  `macro_rules!` macro that defines operations, routes or tools;
- a code generator of its own, including a generated Rust HTTP client;
- a portable query layer, meaning any abstraction that lets one query run on
  more than one database backend;
- a wrapper type around an `axum`, `rmcp` or `sqlx` type in a public API. The
  project passes `sc_runtime::Daemon::builder()` an ordinary
  `utoipa_axum::OpenApiRouter` and an ordinary `rmcp` service.","statements":[{"modal":"Must","text":"For each job in the Job/Crate table, `crates/` and `template/` MUST reuse the listed crate's capability through its documented API, except where a governing requirement or explicit amendment specifies another implementation."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"The repository MUST NOT contain, in `crates/` or in `template/`, the items in the prohibited list in this record’s Requirement Statement, subject to the amendments stated there."}]},"rationale":"Each item in the prohibited list would be code this project has to maintain
and every generated project has to learn, where a standard crate already does
the job and is already documented. Standard designs are preferred over
hand-rolled pieces throughout. The decision that standard designs are
preferred, and that this item and [NFR-RUN-0004](requirements.md) enforce it,
is recorded in [ADR-RUN-0008](architecture.md).","success_criteria":{"text":"1. `grep -rn "proc-macro" --include=Cargo.toml crates template` prints

   framework builds the parts and the project wires them in ordinary Rust. It
   reports no registry type, no generator and no public newtype or trait
   whose only purpose is to hide an `axum`, `rmcp` or `sqlx` type.

   `utoipa_axum::routes!` on an `OpenApiRouter`, the example MCP tools use
   `#[tool]` and `#[tool_router]`, and the CLI uses `clap` derive.

criteria.undefined acronym: An acronym that is never expanded or defined. Fix: define the acronym.

s3_joined_by.instructions: Judge only record.requirement_statement.statements entry 3 (one-based), using the complete record as context. What joins its obligations?

criteria.none: One obligation; nothing is joined.
criteria.and-list: A list of items joined by and or commas. Fix: split into one statement per item.
criteria.condition+obligation: A condition (when, if, unless) plus one obligation. Acceptable: a condition is not a second obligation.
criteria.alternatives: Alternatives joined by or. Fix: split, or state the choice.
criteria.obligation+rationale: An obligation plus its reason or purpose. Fix: move the rationale to Rationale.

diag_01_defect.instructions: What is the primary writing defect in the identified statements?

criteria.reference: A pronoun or cross-reference is ambiguous.
criteria.term: A term or acronym is undefined.
criteria.vague: A qualifier lacks a testable meaning.
criteria.rationale: A reason is mixed into an obligation.
criteria.none: No defect remains when the whole record is read.

diag_02_phrase.instructions: Which specific phrase most needs correction?

criteria.none: None of these phrases needs correction.

diag_03_definition.instructions: Does the record already define that phrase sufficiently?

criteria.yes: Yes, its meaning is already clear in this record.
criteria.partial: Partly, but it still leaves a material ambiguity.
criteria.no: No sufficient definition exists here.

diag_04_edit.instructions: What is the smallest effective correction?

criteria.split: Split independent obligations, repeating scope and conditions.
criteria.name: Replace the pronoun or indirect reference with its actual subject.
criteria.define: Add a local definition from existing record content.
criteria.outcome: State the concrete desired outcome already supported by this record.
criteria.move: Move a reason to Rationale without removing it.
criteria.none: No edit is justified.

diag_05_source.instructions: Which part of the existing material supplies the correction?

criteria.context: The Requirement Statement context or table.
criteria.rationale: The Rationale.
criteria.linked: A requirement or ADR explicitly linked here.
criteria.missing: No existing source specifies the missing meaning.

diag_06_guard.instructions: Which material detail is most at risk of accidental loss in a rewrite?

criteria.enumeration: A listed field, case or item.
criteria.none: No special loss risk is apparent.

diag_07_tightening.instructions: Can a concrete outcome already stated in this record replace the vague wording and make it testable? Tightening around that desired outcome is permitted; invented constraints are not.

criteria.yes: The record already supplies a concrete outcome for a faithful or desirable tightening.
criteria.partial: Only part of the outcome is supplied.
criteria.no: A new substantive decision is required.

diag_08_measure.instructions: Does correction require a new numerical threshold?

criteria.not_needed: No numerical threshold is needed; existing named behavior can be stated precisely.
criteria.existing: A relevant numerical measure already appears in the record.
criteria.new: A new numerical threshold would have to be chosen.
criteria.unclear: The record does not determine this.

diag_09_context.instructions: Is the earlier reported defect a misread of information already present in this complete record?

criteria.yes: The record already supplies the relevant material clearly.
criteria.partial: Relevant material exists but the statement does not connect it clearly.
criteria.no: The relevant material is actually missing or vague.

diag_10_check.instructions: What concrete check best verifies the corrected outcome?

criteria.cli: A CLI invocation with output or exit-code checks.
criteria.files: Inspect the named source or configuration files.
criteria.graph: Inspect the dependency graph or manifests.
criteria.decision: The desired outcome must first be specified.
